source.title: Attention with Markov: A Curious Case of Single-layer Transformers
source.authors: A. Makkuva; Marco Bondaschi; Adway Girish; Alliot Nagle; Martin Jaggi; Hyeji Kim; Michael Gastpar

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed generalization on synthetic Markov-chain data using test-loss trajectories, a different task and measure from the original grokking studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-loss outcomes on Markov-chain next-token prediction. It does not report training accuracy, test accuracy, or a training-set-size sweep. Numerical curve values are not stated in the text. Results cited from other work were not included.
record.test_reason: The study analyses the loss landscape of transformers trained on Markov-chain data. Its test loss is effectively population loss on freshly sampled sequences, so there is no memorization phase, no train–test gap and no training-set size. Grokking is never studied; Nanda et al. is cited only as mechanistic-interpretability work. No result bears on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors prove that weight-tied single-layer transformers have a global minimum (the bigram) for all (p,q) and a bad unigram local minimum when p+q>1, which becomes a saddle without tying. Empirically, some tied runs with p+q>1 get stuck, while runs without tying converge. Depth ≥2 models always reach the global minimum after a unigram plateau.
record.recipe_differences: Uses synthetic first-order Markov-chain next-token prediction and studies transformer loss landscapes, rather than modular arithmetic grokking and its accuracy trajectory.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with Markov switching probabilities, weight tying, depth, and (in the multi-state experiments) state count.

fits_no_version.finding: Transformers of depth ≥2 first plateau at the unigram loss H(π), then drop to the bigram loss after a few iterations. Single-layer weight-tied models with p+q>1 can stay stuck at the unigram minimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss plateaus at simpler-statistic solutions (unigram before bigram) during transformer training on Markov data; escape depends on depth and weight tying. This is an optimization plateau, not delayed generalization.

record.problems: The evidence relevant to delayed generalization is largely test-loss trajectories; training accuracy, test accuracy, and training-set-size dependence are not reported. Several plotted condition-specific values are not described numerically in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately reported outcomes bearing on V1 were left out. The predicted probabilities in Figure 3 are not separate rows because they report the final learned transition or unigram probabilities, not the delayed-generalization trajectory.

untested.parts: All of it: no train/test accuracy, no memorization phase, no training-set-size sweep.
All of it; weight decay is fixed at 1e-3 and not varied.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V1 limits_scope label are wrong. The paper is not about grokking: there is no finite training set to memorize, so 'delayed generalization' cannot arise. Its only link is the depth≥2 plateau-then-drop, which is a training-loss dynamics phenomenon.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report training accuracy saturation, chance-level test accuracy, near-perfect test accuracy, or how delay changes with training-set size. It reports test loss, not test accuracy.
No generalizing circuit, memorizing component, or continuous circuit-progress measure is analyzed.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
Weight tying is varied, but the paper does not test a low-norm efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
The study does not identify or compare learned algorithms across runs.
No adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point softmax artifact is tested.

rows.subject: single-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on binary first-order Markov-chain next-token prediction; report test loss over iterations.
rows.baseline: bigram/global-minimum loss; unigram loss is also shown
rows.value: The model gets stuck at a local minimum corresponding to the unigram distribution.
rows.locator: Figure 1 and its caption; Sections 1 and 4
rows.note: The text describes the loss outcome, but does not report training or test accuracy for this run.
rows.check: A single-layer model stuck at a unigram local minimum is an optimization outcome, not delayed generalization after memorization.

rows.subject: transformers with depth two and beyond (reported collectively)
rows.operation_detail: Train on binary first-order Markov-chain next-token prediction; report test loss over iterations.
rows.value: The loss first plateaus at the unigram loss, then falls to the global minimum after a few additional iterations.
rows.note: The paper reports the pattern collectively for depth two and beyond; it does not give training or test accuracy.
rows.check: A unigram plateau then drop for depth ≥2 is a loss-plateau escape without any train–test gap; record under fits_no_version, not V1.
